deities: Karthyayani (Kathyayani) Devi - anjanashila idol, worshipped in five forms: Saraswati, Lakshmi, Parvathi, Durga and Vana Durga
festivals: Thrikkarthika Utsavam - 10-day annual festival in Vrishchikam (mid November-mid December); 9th day is Devi's birthday

history.dynasty: Cheraman Perumal (per the temple's own history); legendary association with Parasurama
history.period: UNVERIFIED - 2400-year age claimed by tradition; 11th-century inscription attested
history.summary: Major Devi shrine at Kumaranalloor, about 4 km from Kottayam town (CSV town corrected from Kottayam). Legend (temple's own history): the shrine was being built to install Subramanya (Kumaran) when a Madurai Meenakshi priest, wrongly accused of theft, sensed Devi's presence; a sudden thick fog was taken as her manifestation, and the Karthyayani form of the Goddess was consecrated instead - the Subramanya idol was later installed at Udayanapuram near Vaikom. The anjanashila idol was, per lore, brought from Vedagiri and installed by a Brahmin sage identified with Parasurama; the priest's family (Madurai Illam) still performs worship. The village was formerly called Thingalkkadu and Indu Kaananam; an 11th-century inscription survives and local tradition holds a Shiva temple was later converted to a Durga temple. Adi Shankaracharya is said to have ranked it first among the Pancha mahakshetrams. Counted among Kerala's 108 Durga temples.

name: Kumaranalloor Devi Temple
town_description: Kumaranalloor is a locality about 4 km west of Kottayam town in central Kerala, part of the Kottayam urban agglomeration near the Meenachil basin. It is an ancient cultural and village centre whose name derives from Kumaran (Subramanya), though the Devi temple now dominates the place. The area retains traditional Kerala village settlement patterns amid the rubber-growing midlands.

travel.road: About 4 km from Kottayam town on SH-1; easily reached by road from Kottayam city

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; November-December during Thrikkarthika Utsavam
visitor_information.opening_hours: 4:00 AM-11:15 AM and 5:00 PM-8:00 PM (verify - reported by secondary temple-guide sources only)
